note: v5 (2026-11-23): the five-section rail. The groups are now the taxonomy the `unlisted` reasons used to bury — Start, Operations, Content & configuration, Specs & docs, Member — in a stable order, and a surface joins the section its family names. The schema did not change; the arrangement did, and the version is how a later edit is a bump plus a diff rather than a silent reinterpretation of the same number. No route was added, removed, renamed or redirected: `data:check` E43 still accounts for every route under app/(mainlayout), and every href drawn here resolved before this version did.

items.note: The admin landing, surfaced 2026-11-23 (nav evaluation F1). It was `unlisted` on the ruling that the account menu's admin door was enough; the rail's job is to name destinations, and a landing no rail row names is the one surface an operator cannot see from the rail. The account-menu door (#1376) stays — this is a second door to one destination, not a replacement, which is the one place that ruling read wrong rather than the ruling itself. `dashboard` is the glyph the member's Start row draws: both rows open a landing.

#542 phase 2 — the hub for its own subtree (users, templates, relationships), first in the section because every other operator surface hangs off it or beside it. Its three children stay unlisted: the hub names the family, and a row per detail list would be that family written twice.
#542 phase 2 — every relationship the platform holds, after the hub that owns the surface.
The Gap across every relationship: the same operator's question, one level up from a single pair.

#542 phase 2 — the one queue a support seat works, and the only row in this section below admin. It sits with the operator surfaces because that is what it is, not with the member's help pair it shared a heading with under #929.

#665 — the review shelf: published artifacts, each with its to-dos and its feedback. It was one of the two staff rows #929 put inside the member's Support group; Operations is the family the nav evaluation named (F2, F5).
Platform health — the second of the two staff rows #929 had put in Support, back beside the surfaces it reports on.
#505 — billing control: the plan each relationship carries, and the owner's comp. A change to a *setting*, which is why it belongs here and not in the operator list.
#507 — the broadcast: a one-off notice to the news list.
#1138 — the transactional-mail override editor: what the product writes to a person. `inbox` is the glyph the console's own mail surface uses; it is not drawn by another row in this section.

#1126 — the CRUD & Permissions matrix: which role may do what. `review` is the checklist glyph and no name in the set draws a table; the review *shelf* is a row in Operations, so the reuse never reads as the same destination inside one section.
#503 — the log every row above it commits into, and last in the section for that reason: an operator reads it after acting.

The brand and audience profile (#906), surfaced 2026-11-23 (nav evaluation F6). It was `unlisted` because the admin notice bar's CTA already opens it on every screen; it is a *configuration* surface, and this section is where a reader looks for one. `relationships` is the glyph this set draws for people, and an audience profile is about people.

#1252 — the project spec. It led the rail in a title-less group of its own under the 2026-11-19 ruling; that group held one row and is dissolved here, because a section header over a single link is a heading doing no work (nav evaluation F3). `needs: stakeholder` is the rung (between member and support), and `capability: spec-read` is the gate the rung cannot express — support outranks a stakeholder and is refused the spec, so the row names both.
#901 — the docs home, which renders the 117-page manifest. Its two railed sub-surfaces are named below it; `/admin/docs/features` stays inside its tree.

The project spec's validation page (#1252), surfaced 2026-11-23 (nav evaluation F4). It was `unlisted` on "the submenu reaches its pages"; the spec's two pages are one family, and a reader asking what is proven should not have to open the home first. Same gate pair as its parent, because the page calls `requireSpecReader()` itself.

The per-PR update ledger, surfaced 2026-11-23 (nav evaluation F4 — "where is the changelog?" had no stable answer from the rail). `audit` is the scroll glyph: a ledger is a log of entries, which is what an operator reads this page for.
The release notes, surfaced 2026-11-23 with the ledger beside it — the two halves of one question. `broadcast` is the megaphone: a release note is the announcement whose entries the ledger records.

#1129 — Start, the signed-in landing: the computed Next Step, the two active relationships and four templates. `exact` because `/dashboard` is a parent path of the rows below it, and a prefix rule would light Start beside every one of them. This is the row #620 removed when the Overview stopped being a destination; it comes back as a different page.
#620 — the relationship and its assessment, in one list. Second since #1129, because the rail now opens on Start.
#620 — one destination, two tabs: the catalogue and what this member owns. /dashboard/library is a 308 to this tab (next.config.mjs).

#1131 — one thread per relationship, last of the member's own work as the v2 rail draws it (Start · My Relationships · Templates · Chat). NOT /chat: that address is the quiz product's conversations, gated to the quiz brand (#300), and it answers 404 on the build this rail belongs to.

The help centre. It is in the member's section because its reader is a member: the 2026-11-23 reorganisation folded the old Support group into this one, and this row plus the contact row below are the help/contact tail of it, not a second workspace.
The first-run tour points at this row (data-tour="help"). Its reader is a member, so the anchor stays on the last row every rung sees.

unlisted.reason: A console child (#478) — one of the three detail lists inside the console hub's tree, reached from `/admin/console`. Family: the console's own subtree; the hub's row is its door.
A console child (#478) — the operator's view of the template catalogue, inside the console hub's tree and reached from it. Family: the console's subtree.
A console child (#478) — the operator's user queue, inside the console hub's tree and reached from it. Family: the console's subtree.
A docs sub-surface (#901) — a feature page inside the docs home's tree, reached from `/admin/docs`, which renders the whole 117-page manifest. Family: the docs home's tree.

The growth model (#1095) — a screen charting a simulated business, kept by the owner's ruling and drawn by no rail row. Family: operator analytics, deliberately URL-only; this entry is where the ruling is written down.
An operator authoring tree — the alignment product's template list, admin-gated, reached from the console hub. Family: the console's subtree, which is older than the hub's own three children.

The published-template catalogue (#146). Family: the member's browse surfaces, reached from the Templates row and from a relationship's own screen; a third door would make the rail a list of form entries.
A failure state in the create flow (#1226) — where a browser lands when a write throws. Family: the create flow's own states, never a destination.

My Assessments (#877) — the session listing, one click from My Relationships, which is the record that owns each session. Family: the member's relationship surfaces; #1129 retired its rail row when Start took the top slot.

The member's billing surface (#1132) — reached from a relationship's own screen and the account menu. Family: the member's own account surfaces. The v2 reference draws Payment as the last rail row; when the document gains that row, this entry is deleted.

The recorded walkthrough (#898) — the signed-out visitor's copy of the story the rail's How It Works row tells inside the app. Family: the public chrome's pages, reached from it; the rail's row is `/dashboard/help`.
The community leaderboard (#175) — gated on `community.leaderboard` and off on the builds this rail ships, so a row would advertise a 404. Family: the quiz product's community surfaces.
Quiz News & Updates — the quiz catalogue's news list. Family: the quiz product's content surfaces; the alignment build's announcements arrive through the broadcast and the marketing chrome.
The palette's view-all page (#156) — the header's search field opens it, and the palette lists the same results. Family: the chrome's own search surface.
The signed-in person's own profile (#164) — reached from the account menu, which is where a person looks for themselves. Family: the account menu's surfaces.

The account support page's shorter address — the rail's Support row is `/dashboard/support`, the workspace surface #542 phase 1 built; this one is the page it replaced and still answers. Family: the shell's legacy addresses.
